Tap the picture to use it like a touch screen. Use Menu to pick phone videos, saved links, YouTube or screen mirroring. On the phone app you can paste links or share videos from YouTube to AutoCarPlay. For your safety, only watch while parked.
Allow AutoCarPlay to read the videos on your phone. Check your phone after tapping the button.

If nothing appears, open AutoCarPlay on the phone and tap “Start mirroring”.
Check your phone to start mirroring
To control the phone from this screen, turn on AutoCarPlay touch control in the phone app (Accessibility).
Touch control is off (enable it in the phone app)

Tap to show your phone screen on the car display.
Mirroring started. Open the app you want to watch (for example YouTube) and turn the phone sideways.
Lets you tap and swipe on the car screen to control the phone while it is mirrored. AutoCarPlay does not read or store anything on your screen.
AutoCarPlay is open on the car screen. Pick something to play below or on the car.
Your video will start as soon as you open AutoCarPlay on the car screen.
Open AutoCarPlay from the Android Auto app launcher on the car screen.
Connect your phone to the car. Do the one-time setup below first.
Choose a video from this phone
Tip: in YouTube or Chrome, tap Share → AutoCarPlay to send a video straight to the car.

Shows your phone screen on the car display, so you can watch any app. Apps that block screen recording (Netflix, Prime Video and similar) show a black picture. Keep the phone unlocked and turn it sideways for a full-screen picture.
Touch control is on: taps on the car screen control the phone.
Touch control is off. Without it, the mirrored screen can only be watched, not tapped.
Find “AutoCarPlay touch control” under Installed apps / Downloaded apps and turn it on.

1. Open Android Auto settings (button below, or phone Settings → Connected devices → Connection preferences → Android Auto).
2. Scroll to the bottom and tap “Version” 10 times, then allow developer settings.
3. Tap ⋮ (top right) → Developer settings → turn on “Unknown sources”.
4. Go back → Customize launcher → make sure AutoCarPlay is ticked.
5. Connect the phone to your car and open AutoCarPlay on the car screen.

Touch control on Android 13+: if Android says the setting is restricted, open phone Settings → Apps → AutoCarPlay → ⋮ → “Allow restricted settings”, then turn it on again.
